summary: Extends L2TP, which tunnels PPP over packet networks, to support ATM SVC- or PVC-based access networks. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: It is an add-on to a tunnel system so it works with another type of network connection called ATM.

questions: what is an l2tp access concentrator
how does l2tp support atm pvc and svc
subtitle: Extra L2TP messages and fields so PPP sessions arriving over ATM circuits can be tunnelled to a network server.

tldr.problem: L2TP was designed mainly for ISDN and PSTN access, but ATM access networks need asymmetric bandwidth, service category selection and ATM addressing.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds a broadband (B) bearer bit and six new AVPs, and changes how number and speed AVPs are used, so an LAC and LNS can set up calls over ATM PVCs or SVCs.
tldr.outcome: It extends RFC 2661 without adding security risks beyond those of that RFC, and asks IANA for six new AVP type values.

facts.label: Service Category mask
facts.value: 16 bits; S bit 0 non-real time, 1 real time

facts.label: IANA request
facts.value: 6 new AVP type values and the B bit

today: RFC 3301 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 2661, which it extends.

sections.title: Introduction and Goals
sections.content:
RFC 2661 defines how L2TP tunnels PPP sessions between an L2TP Access Concentrator (LAC) and an L2TP Network Server (LNS), with a focus on HDLC based ISDN and PSTN access networks. This RFC augments those procedures to support ATM access networks based on switched virtual circuits (SVC) or permanent virtual circuits (PVC).

ATM needs three things beyond RFC 2661: handling of traffic management (asymmetric bandwidth and service category selection), the addressing format of switched ATM networks, and the limits on LCP negotiation when PPP runs over AAL5 as in RFC 2364. This RFC covers the first two. The third is not ATM specific and is left to a separate work in progress, L2TP Link Extensions.
sections.plainLanguage: The old tunnel only knew about phone-line connections. ATM connections need extra details, such as how fast in each direction, so this document adds them.

sections.title: Setting Up the Connection and Tunnel
sections.content:
Before PPP starts, a virtual connection MUST be set up between the user and the LAC. It is either a preconfigured PVC or an on-demand SVC negotiated through ATM signalling. The user is called the virtual dial-in user. For a PVC the LAC may be triggered by an LCP Configure Request or a PPP authentication request, though exact timing is outside the scope.

If no tunnel to the chosen LNS exists, one is created. During tunnel establishment the bearer capability is extended so the LAC can say it supports ATM. Only once the LNS sees that indication can both sides use these extensions. If the LAC and LNS are not compatible, no tunnel can be established, but implementations are encouraged to fall back gracefully to digital bearer capability.

The RFC does not negotiate the signalling-specific information elements of switched VC service over the tunnel. Instead it identifies the connection with ATM end system addresses, and for PVCs also allows a textual Service Name.
sections.plainLanguage: First the person and the access box make a link. Then the access box opens a tunnel to the server and says it can speak ATM. If the server cannot, they try the older way.

sections.title: Incoming and Outgoing Calls
sections.content:
In an incoming call the LAC sends an ICRQ. It MUST indicate a broadband bearer by setting the B bit in the Bearer Type AVP, and MAY include the Service Category and Service Name AVPs and the VPI/VCI identifier AVP. If the LNS does not support the B bit it returns an error and the sides MAY fall back to digital bearer. In the ICCN, the Tx and Rx Connect Speed AVPs SHOULD be used when the connection is asymmetric.

In an outgoing call the LNS sends an OCRQ. It MUST give the minimum and maximum receive and transmit speeds from the LAC's point of view, and to support UBR connections the Minimum BPS MUST be zero. It MAY add a Service Category saying real time or non-real time. Real time can be met by CBR or rt-VBR, and non-real time by UBR, nrt-VBR, ABR or GFR. The called number MUST be in the NSAP format; if it is all zeros, the LAC SHOULD use the Service Name to pick the ATM VC. The OCRP MAY contain the VPI/VCI identifier AVP.

For framing, the LAC strips the AAL5 fields from user traffic, according to the encapsulation in use (VC multiplexed or LLC encapsulated), and adds HDLC-style address and control fields for the tunnel. In the other direction it does the reverse.
sections.plainLanguage: When the access box starts a call it says 'this is an ATM call'. When the server starts one it says how fast it wants each direction and whether it must be real time, such as for live talking.

sections.title: New AVPs
sections.content:
Six new AVPs are defined. All have the M bit set to 0 and may be hidden. Their usage is limited to cases where the LAC indicated broadband bearer support during tunnel establishment.

  • Rx Minimum BPS (40) and Rx Maximum BPS (41): 32-bit speeds in bits per second for the receive direction (user to LAC), used in OCRQ. Length 10.
  • Service Category (42): a 16-bit mask where the S bit means real time when 1 and non-real time when 0. Other bits are reserved. Used in OCRQ and ICRQ. Length 8.
  • Service Name (43): a UTF-8 text name for a preestablished PVC, at least 1 octet, to be unique at least for the LNS/LAC pair. It may only be given when the OCRQ called number is all zeros.
  • Calling Sub-Address (44): a 20 octet binary NSAP subaddress, used in ICRQ. Length 26.
  • VPI/VCI identifier (45): a 32 bit value with 12 bits of VPI and 16 bits of VCI, used in ICRQ and OCRP. Length 10.
sections.plainLanguage: These are new labelled boxes in the messages: how slow or fast each way, real time or not, a nickname for the circuit, and its exact circuit numbers.

sections.title: Changes to Existing AVPs
sections.content:
The Bearer Capabilities and Bearer Type AVPs gain a B bit meaning broadband (ATM) access; the A bit means analogue and the D bit digital. In an OCRQ all three bits may be set. If a call is attempted with bearer type B but the capability was not indicated, it is rejected with Result Code 5. An LNS that does not understand the B bit is expected to treat the AVP as unrecognized, so tunnel establishment fails with Result Code 2 and Error Code 3.

When the B bit is set in the Bearer Type AVP, the Called Number (type 21), Calling Number (22) and Sub-Address (23) AVPs MUST be encoded as 20 octet binary NSAP addresses, structured as in the ATM Forum addressing guide (E.164, ICD, DCC). Each has length 26. The (Tx) Minimum and Maximum BPS AVPs keep their meaning, but if the matching Rx AVP is absent, symmetric transmission is implied. The Q.931 Cause Code AVP may also carry ATM signalling cause codes, interpreted relative to the bearer type.
sections.plainLanguage: The old fields still work, but when the call is ATM, addresses are written in a longer, fixed-size format. If a side does not understand ATM, the tunnel is refused rather than half-working.

sections.title: Authentication, Authorization and Security
sections.content:
For switched VCs, the calling party number may be used for first-level authentication, as with PSTN or ISDN access. For PVCs, authentication may not matter on the LAC side because the circuit is permanent, and a bilateral agreement between LAC and LNS providers may skip the authentication phase.

Because ATM connections can be set up with varying parameters, some authorization may be needed before accepting a switched connection with certain traffic parameters. Requests that are not authorized result in connection release. The Security Considerations section says no extra security risk beyond those of RFC 2661 is foreseen.
sections.plainLanguage: The server may check who is calling and whether they are allowed to ask for that kind of connection. If not, the connection is closed.

fields.name: VPI
fields.desc: Virtual Path Identifier at the LAC ATM interface.

fields.name: VCI
fields.desc: Virtual Channel Identifier at the LAC ATM interface.

items.label: Service Category
items.desc: Real time or non-real time (OCRQ, ICRQ).

items.label: Service Name
items.desc: Text name of a preestablished PVC (OCRQ, ICRQ).

items.label: VPI/VCI identifier
items.desc: VPI and VCI at the LAC (ICRQ, OCRP).
